summary.subject: Recovery: lexer.LexRecover and parser.ParseRecover go on past errors, for an editor, and return them all in source order, the first being the one the strict path reports; a string or template left open ends where the error is, a bad escape is kept as written, unreadable source becomes a Bad token, and malformed markup is read as far as it goes, an end tag that names an enclosing element closing it as a browser would; the parser resyncs at the next statement, list item, or interpolation, restoring the nesting it left, puts a BadStmt, BadExpr, or BadType where nothing could be read, an empty one just after the last token so it lies in its node, reads a dangling dot as a field with no name, a var or type without its initializer or body, a list closed by the end of the file, a brace that ends an enclosing block, or a statement on a line of its own, and a block closed by the end of the file; loader.Config.Recover keeps every module it can read with its source and layout, marks an import it cannot follow with Module -1, and returns the program with the diagnostics; the resolver and checker accept Bad nodes and the names of a missing module without a word; tests: the recovering paths agree with the strict ones on every valid corpus file, report every strict error, never panic on any prefix of the corpus cut at token boundaries, build sound spans, and the checker gives the same diagnostics on a recovered program as on a strict one
